editorial:
Imagine taking a trip to the city of lights with a curious girl who always finds herself in weird situations. You get to follow Alice as she explores Paris, but instead of one long plot, you get a collection of five short, sweet stories. It feels like sitting down with a big book of fairy tales while someone reads to you. The vibe is very light and playful, making it a great pick if you want something that feels like a warm hug. It is less about a big adventure and more about the small, magical moments that happen in these children's stories.

What really pops is the art style, which looks like the picture books actually came to life on screen. The pacing is quick because the stories change often, so you never get bored. While some of the older animation might feel a bit simple today, the charm makes up for it. You should definitely check this out if you have kids or just want a nostalgic break. For the best experience, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection to keep those colors bright. It is a cozy watch that works perfectly for a rainy afternoon.
endingExplained: After Alice finishes hearing all five stories, the movie wraps up by bringing her back to her own world. There is no giant twist or shocking ending because it is an anthology. The final scenes show Alice reflecting on the lessons learned from the characters like Madeline and Anatole. She leaves Paris feeling happier and more imaginative, closing the loop on her journey and leaving you with a peaceful, happy feeling.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic children's books and relaxing stories.
